evidence: James T. Palmer's university bibliography confirms The Apocalypse in the Early Middle Ages, Anglo-Saxons in a Frankish World, Early Medieval Hagiography and the early-medieval articles (about 31/36 weighted citations). The Bloody White Baron is the journalist's; Roman Peacemaking is James A. Palmer's; Dieselgate is the geographer's.

José Filipe Pinto's university bibliography confirms Segredos do Império da Ilusitânia and Do Império Colonial à Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa (4/20 weighted citations). Pina Manique is by Adérito Tavares and José dos Santos Pinto; Curso de direito individual do trabalho is José Augusto Rodrigues Pinto's. The remaining titles do not establish further Filipe Pinto authorship.

The authority anchors identify Marc David Baer, the Ottoman historian. Honored by the Glory of Islam, The Dönme and the Ottoman articles account for 22/33 weighted citations. Theatre and Disorder, Political Dinners, Radical Westminster and Victorian London belong to the separate Hope College historian Marc Baer.

The Library of Congress identifies Following the Color Line, Woodrow Wilson and World Settlement, Woodrow Wilson: Life and Letters and American Chronicle as Ray Stannard Baker's; his journalism also fits the listed labor and race articles. English-Canadian Literature, the Rensselaer history and Poetry of Jacob Bailey belong to Ray Palmer Baker. The malformed French title remains unresolved.

William Donald Coleman's university bibliography confirms The Independence Movement in Quebec, Business and Politics, Financial Services and Fifty Key Thinkers. His policy-network articles and coedited Empires and Autonomy, including the truncated Vancouver entry, bring his share to about 19/24. Doing Masculinity/Doing Theory is Wil Coleman's; the Cajuns article credits W. H. Coleman.

The key identifies the military journalist, author with Bernard Trainor of The Generals' War and Cobra II. Those books, the 2006 newspaper article and probably the translation fragment supply about 7/26 weighted citations. Conflict and Consensus in Labour's Foreign Policy (including two fragments) and Domestic Conflict and the Origins of the First World War belong to the political scientist namesake.

David Gary Shaw's CV confirms Necessary Conjunctions, Creation of a Community, Modernity Between Us and Them, Torturer's Horse, Happy in Our Chains, Social Networks and his Historical Animal chapter (19/27 weighted citations). Mendham, Sinapius and the incunable work are David J. Shaw's; Arthurian Ghosts is David W. Shaw's; the reporting and sports titles introduce further namesakes.

John Russell Bartlett wrote or edited Rhode Island Records, Personal Narrative (both entries), Dictionary of Americanisms, the Russell genealogy and Roger Williams's Letters: about 14/23 weighted citations. Maccabees, Jews in the Hellenistic World and biblical archaeology belong to John Raymond Bartlett. This is a mixed ID with a modest LC majority, below the brief's roughly two-thirds mostly threshold; the categorical verdict is therefore uncertain.

Getzel M. Cohen wrote the three Hellenistic Settlements volumes, The Seleucid Colonies, Katoikiai and Colonization and Population Transfer; together with the Seleucid bibliographic fragment these supply about 34/42 weighted citations. The equality book, Future of a Disillusion and Reply to Elster are G. A. Cohen's; the displaced-persons chapter is Gerard Daniel Cohen's.

Nancy C. Cox is the retail historian responsible for The Complete Tradesman, Perceptions of Retailing, Dictionary of Traded Goods, Probate and the other early-modern material (about 21/25 weighted citations). The three influenza works credit virologist Nancy J. Cox. The Royal Prerogative and Constitutional Law is by Noel Cox.
